v.rationale: All three work the same way. Files go on the private 'local' disk under hashed names. Links are temporary signed URLs to an unauthenticated download route that sends the file as an attachment. Each checks that the file exists both when issuing the link and on download, and another user gets a 404. All suites pass: impl-2 18 tests, impl-3 15, impl-1 14. I ran the same probes on all three, and each gave identical results. A non-ASCII filename containing '%' downloads correctly with an RFC 5987 Content-Disposition header. Real uploaded files with text or HTML content but a .pdf or .png name are rejected because the content is sniffed. A real PDF named .php is rejected. A user_id sent in the request is ignored. Appending a query parameter to a signed URL gives 403, and a deleted document gives 404. No functional bugs, so the ranking comes down to idioms. impl-3 is best: fluent File::types rule, authorization at the route with ->can and denyAsNotFound, and a bounded original_name. impl-2 is nearly identical, with Gate::authorize in the controller, string mimes rules and slightly more granular tests. impl-1 comes last: inline validation, a manual ownership check instead of a policy, and user_id left mass-assignable on the model.
